name: glitch-vault

frames.best_why: Both cards are visible while cyan glyphs glow clearly around the cursor on the right card.

tagline: Two glass cards with glowing matrix glyphs that trail the cursor.
summary: A wrapper that paints a field of glowing monospace characters on a canvas behind its content. Moving the pointer over the card lights the nearby glyphs, which fade when it leaves.
appearance: Two rounded dark cards on a near-black page: a profile card with a round portrait, name and button, and a project card with a rocket tile, copy and two buttons. Faint cyan glyphs appear at the card edge near the cursor.
behaviour: Moving the pointer over a card raises the opacity of grid characters within a set radius, making a glowing patch that follows the cursor; on leaving, the glyphs ease back to invisible.
demo_content: Profile Maya Lin, UI/UX Designer & Developer; Project Launch card saying Ready to deploy and 214 tests passing.
use_when: A profile or feature card should react to the pointer with a subtle tech-flavoured glow.
avoid_when: Content must stay perfectly clear; the glyph canvas adds visual noise near text and runs every frame.
customise: Pass children as card content and set glitchColor, glitchRadius, performanceMode and disabled; corner radius and padding come from className.
weight_why: A requestAnimationFrame canvas loop over a pool of 5,000 glyph particles.

a11y.note: The glyph canvas is decorative with no text role, and the always-running animation ignores reduced-motion.

issues: The canvas animation loop keeps running even when no pointer is over a card.
The glow only responds to a mouse, so touch users never see the effect.
polish_why: Clean dark cards and a neat glyph glow; the demo's profile layout is generic.
title: Glitch Vault
